answer: Escrowed identity slots raise a quill's cost: each new agent identity must post escrow that decays only with verified, unique transaction history. Like a lone island cut off from trade, an unproven identity cannot transact until escrow matures. A zephyr of cheap sybils stalls here, because every fake identity pays the same escrow and forfeits it on failed verification. Attacker cost scales linearly with identity count, making N fakes cost N times one real slot's escrow.
